input: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Peloton expected to price its $600M of senior secured notes due 2032, its first high-yield bond, in the week of Nov 9, 2026. Bloomberg, via Investing.com, reported yield talk in the low-to-mid 9% range, with Goldman Sachs leading. The proceeds plus cash on hand will repay and end the $1.0B term loan. A new $200M five-year revolver is also proposed.

The holiday quarter (Q2 FY27) depends heavily on Black Friday, Cyber Monday and the winter holidays, and management said this limits how far ahead it can see. Q2 guidance is revenue of $625M–$650M, adjusted EBITDA of $85M–$100M and gross margin of about 50%.

Q2 FY27 results are expected in early February 2027, but the date has not been announced. This is an inference from last year: Peloton announced its Q2 FY26 date on Jan 22, 2026 and reported on Feb 5, 2026.

A ruling is pending in the NEC patent case. A jury awarded NEC $20.5M in past damages on July 31, 2026. Peloton has filed a renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law, NEC is seeking ongoing royalties or an injunction, and briefing finished on Oct 20, 2026.

Holders of the 5.50% convertible notes due 2029 cannot convert through Dec 31, 2026. After that date conversion may become possible, subject to the indenture's conditions. The conversion price is about $4.58, below the stock's $5.61 on Nov 6. Peloton can redeem the notes for cash from Jun 7, 2027, subject to a stock-price condition.

The new Tread lineup (Tread Flex, Tread Vision, Tread+ Vision) launched in North America first, with other markets following in spring 2027. Peloton plans hardware in a new product category for fall 2027.

In the 2023 securities class action, which was dismissed with prejudice on Mar 31, 2026, plaintiffs have appealed to the Second Circuit and filed their brief on Aug 14, 2026. In a separate SDNY class action, plaintiffs asked for leave to amend on Sep 28, 2026 after their complaint was dismissed on Aug 27, 2026.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q1 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2026): revenue was $559.2M, up 2% YoY and about $4M above the guidance midpoint of about $555M. Subscription revenue was $410.7M (+3%) and Connected Fitness Products revenue was $148.5M (-3%). This was the third straight quarter of YoY revenue growth.
Against consensus, diluted EPS was $0.19 vs $0.11 expected and revenue was $559.2M vs $553.46M expected. The stock still fell 0.9% to $5.61 on Nov 6, on 13.15M shares against a 7.41M average.

Gross margin was 61.3% vs about 57% guided. Product gross margin was 33.4% (6.9% a year earlier) and subscription gross margin was 71.3%. Adjusted EBITDA was $167.8M (+42% YoY), GAAP net income was $96M and free cash flow was $143M (+113%).

Earnings quality: about $25M of the beat came from tariff and recall-related items that management called nonrecurring. Excluding them, adjusted EBITDA was about $143M, roughly $3M above the guidance midpoint.

Paid Connected Fitness subscriptions were 2.475M (-9% YoY, -3% QoQ), at the top of guidance. Average net monthly churn was 1.7% (1.6% a year earlier, 2.2% in Q4 FY26). Paid app subscriptions were 0.487M (-10%) and members were 5.3M (-11%).

Q2 FY27 guidance: revenue of $625M–$650M (about -3% YoY at the midpoint), ending paid CF subscriptions of 2.425M–2.445M, gross margin of about 50.0% (-50 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $85M–$100M (about +14% at the midpoint vs $81.4M).

FY27 guidance was unchanged: revenue of $2.30B–$2.40B (about -4% at the midpoint vs FY26's $2,446.0M), gross margin of about 54.0%, adjusted EBITDA of $475M–$525M (FY26: $468.2M) and free cash flow of at least $350M (FY26: $377.6M). Management expects FY27 churn to be roughly flat YoY.
Comparisons get harder from here. Q1 was the last quarter compared against the period before the October 2025 subscription price increase, and Peloton starts lapping that increase midway through Q2.

event_driven.claim: On Nov 9, 2026 Peloton launched a global refinancing: $600M of senior secured notes due 2032 plus a proposed $200M five-year revolver, to fully repay the $1.0B term loan. Any leftover proceeds may go to general corporate purposes, including possible share repurchases.

No buyback program has been announced. The CFO said capital return will be reviewed with the board, weighing returns, risks and liquidity. Repurchases are only one possible use of leftover refinancing proceeds and are not committed.
The 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 30, 2026 does not mention any share repurchase authorization or repurchases.

Growth initiatives: Commercial business unit revenue grew 13% YoY in Q1 (Peloton estimates about 4% share of commercial fitness equipment), and the Peloton Commercial Series is now on sale. Peloton has 19 US Micro Stores, about double last year, and Fitness Factory is its first Canada-specific retail partner.

credit_signals.claim: At Sep 30, 2026 Peloton had cash and equivalents of $1,342.2M and restricted cash of $40.3M. The $100M revolver (due May 30, 2029) was undrawn. Its covenants (minimum liquidity of $250M; trailing subscription revenue of $1.2B) are tested only when the revolver is drawn.

Term loan (due May 30, 2029; SOFR+6.00%; effective rate 10.5%): $977.5M outstanding at Sep 30, 2026. A voluntary $280M prepayment on Oct 9, 2026 cut it to $697.5M. The 2026 convertible notes were repaid in cash ($199.0M) in Feb 2026.
Gross principal debt is $1.048B after the October paydown, down 32% from $1.534B at Dec 31, 2025.

First credit ratings: S&P rates Peloton BB- (stable) and the notes and revolver BB, with a '2' recovery rating. It expects leverage of about 2.3x–2.7x in FY27–28 (3.3x in FY26) and would consider a downgrade at 4.0x. Moody's rates the notes Ba3 (stable) with an SGL-1 liquidity rating. It puts pro forma debt/EBITDA at about 3.9x and pro forma cash at about $814M plus the undrawn $200M revolver.

The 5.50% convertible notes due Dec 1, 2029 ($350.0M) remain outstanding and are not part of the refinancing. Their conversion price is about $4.58 (218.4360 shares per $1,000), which implies about 76M shares if fully converted (our calculation). They are the nearest significant maturity after the refinancing.

Management said it would be 'patient' and 'methodical' on the refinancing because credit markets have been volatile since late August. It described the ratings process and investor meetings as complete, with positive feedback.

alternative_signals.claim: Peloton cut about 11% of its workforce on Jan 30, 2026, mainly in engineering. Reported headcounts differ: about 286 in one source, 400 in another.

The 2025 Restructuring Plan was substantially complete by Jun 30, 2026, with no material further charges expected. Q1 FY27 restructuring was a $(1.0)M net benefit. Q1 operating expenses were $226.2M, down 7% YoY.

Pricing: the new treadmill entry model costs $1,000 less than the previous base model, made possible by hardware cost cuts and more suppliers. Tread Flex, the first foldable Peloton tread, is priced near $2,000.

Tariffs: Peloton received refunds for substantially all IEEPA tariffs after the Supreme Court struck them down on Feb 20, 2026, and booked them as lower product cost. New Section 301 tariffs of 10.0%–12.5% on goods from about 60 economies took effect Jul 24, 2026. Section 232 tariffs no longer apply to fitness equipment from Apr 6, 2026.
Engagement: Pilates workouts rose 53% YoY. Peloton had 19 Micro Stores against a goal of 20 by the holidays. The new treads went on sale Oct 1, 2026.

Morgan Stanley's channel and market view: Peloton's share of consumer bikes, treads and rowers has fallen to about 9% from a 38% COVID-era peak, against about 45% of connected fitness. The bank doubts consensus expectations that gross adds will rise 36% over three years.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig sold 10,000 shares at an average of $5.45 (about $54.5K) on Oct 20, 2026 under a 10b5-1 plan and holds 257,729 shares. MarketBeat counts 217,712 shares (about $1.18M) of insider sales last quarter and puts insider ownership at about 1.30%.

Director and former interim co-CEO Karen Boone sold 25,000 shares at a weighted average of $5.35 (about $134K) on Aug 17, 2026 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Aug 13, 2025. She holds about 236,063 shares directly.

CEO Peter Stern's 2026 Form 4 disposals were sales or share withholding to cover taxes on vesting RSUs, not discretionary open-market sales. For example, about 30,484 shares were withheld when RSUs vested in Aug 2026. No insider open-market buying was found.
Shares outstanding at Nov 2, 2026: 430,013,953 Class A and 15,836,474 Class B.

Sell-side: the consensus is Hold (5 Buy / 7 Hold / 1 Sell) with an average target of $7.60. Canaccord cut its target to $8 from $10 (Oct 30), Goldman reiterated Buy, Telsey reiterated Market Perform, and Morgan Stanley is Underweight with a $4.50 target.

risks.claim: The subscriber base keeps shrinking. Paid CF subscriptions fell 9% YoY to 2.475M, guidance implies about 2.435M at the Q2 midpoint, and members are down 11% YoY.

The Q1 margin beat flattered results. About $25M of tariff and recall benefits will not recur, and revenue growth from the price increase fades once it is lapped from mid-Q2. FY27 revenue is guided down about 4%.

Dilution: the $350M convertible notes convert at about $4.58, below the current share price, so they are in the money. That could add up to about 76M shares (our calculation), roughly 17% of the 446M shares outstanding.

Legal and regulatory: NEC is seeking ongoing royalties or an injunction after its $20.5M jury verdict. The DOJ and DHS have subpoenaed documents on Peloton's Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA) obligations. A Nov 2025 seat-post recall covers about 833K US and 44.8K Canadian Bike+ units.

Refinancing execution: yield talk in the low-to-mid 9% range shows high-yield funding costs. Management has pointed to credit-market volatility since late August, and the notes had not priced as of Nov 9.
Moody's expects FY27 revenue down about 8% and pro forma debt/EBITDA of about 3.7x–4.0x, close to S&P's 4.0x downgrade threshold. Both are more cautious than company guidance.
Tariffs on hardware are back: Section 301 tariffs of 10.0%–12.5% on goods from about 60 economies took effect Jul 24, 2026.

output.research_view: PTON is now a cash-generating business that is shrinking slowly. Q1 FY27 brought $143M of free cash flow, $1.34B of cash at Sep 30 and full-year guidance held, but paid subscriptions are falling about 9% a year and much of the Q1 beat came from nonrecurring tariff and recall items. The near-term driver is the debut $600M secured-bond refinancing (S&P BB-, Moody's Ba3), whose pricing should come this week and could free cash for possible buybacks, followed by holiday-quarter demand for the cheaper Tread lineup, which will show up in early-February Q2 results. The main things to watch are whether churn stays flat for the year, whether gross adds stabilize, and the in-the-money 2029 convertible notes, which could add about 17% to the share count.

Confirmed Q2 FY27 earnings date (not yet announced; early February is an inference from last year)
